sonnet.problem: The question says Paul calls it "the fullness of the Deity" and then asks "How much of it?" The word "fullness" already rules out "Most of it" and "Just a part of it," so the question gives the answer away.
sonnet.rule: A choice card's question never holds its own answer, or a form of it, like "rock badgers" for "in the rocks." Ask something else.

sonnet.problem: The statement repeats the right answer of card 5 ("They were raised with Him") and adds only the faith and power-of-God wording from the same verse. It re-asks a fact the baker has just answered, so it is not a new question.
sonnet.rule: An easy follow-up asks something new. It never re-asks the same fact. Two lines that make the same point get one question. An answer shown on one card, right or wrong, isn't used again on a later card.

sonnet.problem: Two of the three answers do not fit the sentence grammatically: "forgave us most our trespasses" and "forgave us some our trespasses" read as broken English. Only "all" fits, so the wrong answers are obviously wrong.
sonnet.rule: Clear English. Every card reads correctly. Each answer fits its question: in a blank, every answer matches the sentence's tense and form, and a "where" question gets places.

sonnet.rule: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage. No recap cards.
